sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:1
items.html:
Explains well the matter of the ten Sefirot of Toch, which are KHB TM extending one above the other, and it has four matters: 1. The first observation is in the Peh of the Rosh, to make the roots of the vessels. The second observation is in the Tabur, to make complete vessels. 2. Although the extension of the level requires the coarsest vessel, nevertheless the light drawn by virtue of that coarseness clothes in the more refined vessel. 3. When the vessel of phase four is refined, the vessel of Malchut is completed, since from the aspect of clothing, phase four is considered Malchut; and when phase three is refined, the vessel of ZA is completed, and so on. 4. After the five vessels of KHB TM were refined and imprinted one above the other, the light returned and clothed in them.

A broad explanation of the ten Sefirot of Toch, which extend one above the other
Now, these things are also brought in the words of the ARI, in Etz Chaim, Heichal AK, Shaar AHP, chapter 3, and he concludes there in this language: "But the vessels for the body, which are the ZAT, still had no power in this vision, until it reached the very soul of the soul, and through the second observation from below upward, which are the light of Akudim and the light of the eye, the light returned and clothed the ZAT." End of quote.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:2
items.html:
Why the second observation is needed for the sake of the vessels
And you see here in the words of the ARI, how he elaborates and is precise, that for the vessels of the Guf, a second observation is needed besides the observation in the Rosh, since two aspects of lights are needed for them, which are the light of Akudim and the light of the eye. At first glance one might ask, why is it not enough for the expansion of the ten Sefirot of reflected light from Malchut downward, in order to bring out the ten Sefirot of the Guf, but a second observation is also needed, and so on.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:3
items.html:
In the first observation only one level of ten Sefirot extended; in the second observation five levels extended, from five couplings, one above the other
Indeed, with what was explained above (chapter 4, item 4), that the ten Sefirot that extend through a coupling by striking at one time, whose level is equal, are considered only a single Sefira, namely, in the name of the uppermost Sefira in that level. It follows from this, that through the first observation, which raised the reflected light from Malchut upward to the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, whose level is equal, and likewise through their expansion from Malchut downward, by which ten Sefirot of an equal level of the Guf extended, there is here still only one Sefira in the Rosh, and one Sefira in the Guf. And you already know that no degree is complete with less than ten Sefirot. Therefore, a second observation is needed, through which ten complete Sefirot extend, which are the five levels of KHB TM, one above the other, through the five couplings of striking that come by virtue of the refinement of the screen, as is written here (in Inner Light, chapter 12, item 8), see there at length.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:4
items.html:
Regarding the clothing of the lights in the vessels, the more refined one is, the greater the light that clothes in it
And you should know, that these five levels, which extend in the Guf through the second observation mentioned above, extend from below upward, so that at first Malchut extends, and afterward ZA, and afterward Bina, and above all of them Keter. And the reason is, according to what was written above (Inner Light, chapter 11, item 3, and in Inner Observation, part 2, under "and this is"), that although the bestowal of the more important level requires a coarser vessel, nevertheless the light drawn by virtue of that coarseness cannot clothe there, since the more important the light is, the more refined the vessel it clothes in, see there the whole passage. It follows from this, that phase four of the vessel of Malchut, although it draws the more important light, namely the level of Keter, nevertheless the light of Keter does not clothe in that vessel of Malchut of phase four, but only in the aspect of the vessel of Malchut fully refined of all coarseness, namely, after it has been refined to the aspect of the root, and so with all of them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:5
items.html:
The vessels extended one above the other, from Malchut to the vessel of Keter
It follows from this, that after Malchut was refined from phase four to phase three, and there remained a vessel of phase four without light, a vessel of Malchut was imprinted here, fit for the lower light, namely, called the light of Nefesh. And afterward, when it was refined from phase three to phase two, and there also remained a vessel of Malchut of phase three without light, a vessel of ZA was imprinted here, fit for the light of Ruach, which is one degree superior to the light of Nefesh. And afterward, when it was refined from phase two to phase one, and phase two in Malchut also remained without light, a vessel of Bina was imprinted here, fit for the light of Neshama. And afterward, when it was refined from phase one to the aspect of the root, and phase one of Malchut also remained without light, a vessel of Hochma was imprinted here, fit for the light of Haya. And the aspect of the root of Malchut is fit for the light of Keter, called the light of Yechida. And after these five vessels were imprinted: KHB, ZA and Malchut, one above the other, the upper light returned and clothed in them, as the ARI wrote (in Etz Chaim, Gate 6, chapter 6).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:6
items.html:
The order for the extension of the lights is the reverse of the order for the clothing of the lights in the vessels. In extension, the coarser is more important. In clothing, the more refined is more important
And you find, that although a coupling of striking on a screen of phase four brings out ten Sefirot at the level of Keter, with the light of Yechida; and likewise, when the portion of coarseness of phase four is refined from Malchut, the level of Keter is found to have disappeared from there; nevertheless, that portion of Malchut of phase four becomes only the aspect of a vessel for the light of Malchut, which is Nefesh. And likewise, the portion of coarseness of phase three in the vessel of Malchut, which through a coupling of striking brings out the level of Hochma with the light of Haya, and likewise when that portion of coarseness of phase three is refined from Malchut, the level of Hochma is found to have disappeared, nevertheless that portion of Malchut of phase three becomes only the aspect of a vessel for the light of ZA, which is Ruach. And likewise the portion of coarseness of phase two becomes a vessel for the light of Neshama. And likewise the portion of coarseness of phase one becomes a vessel for the light of Haya. And the portion in it that is refined to the aspect of the root becomes a vessel for the light of Yechida.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:7
items.html:
Through the second observation, five vessels of KHB TM were made
Thus, through the second observation, which occurs at the time of the refinement of the screen, five vessels extend and are made one above the other, so that at first Malchut extends, and afterward ZA, and afterward Bina, and afterward Hochma, and afterward Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:8
items.html: And this is what the ARI wrote, "that through the second observation from below upward, which are the light of Akudim and the light of the eye, the light returned and clothed the ZAT." He means to say, that through the second observation at the time of the refinement of the screen, which proceeds to make four couplings of striking from below upward, the ten Sefirot are found to be proceeding to clothe the ZAT. Namely, for the light of the Guf of the Partzuf, called the seven lower ones, as will be written before us.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 6:9
items.html:
The ten Sefirot that extend from the Peh to the Tabur are called Akudim, and the light that extends for the coupling of striking is called observation
And this is what he said, "which are the light of Akudim and the light of the eye." For the five portions of Malchut mentioned above, found from the Malchut of the Rosh to the Malchut of Malchut, are called "Akudim," for the reason that all these lights are bound in one vessel, namely in Malchut, since they are all only portions of Malchut, as above. And the light that extends for striking in the secret of the second observation mentioned is called the light of the eye.
